Results and limits

modeled

The station-fed pipe reached both reef docks, then struck the receiver during ejection

The same pipe stayed in the four-pin capture through the observed stops at 56.10 and 55.21 seconds. A 337 mm extension left at least 2.71 mm of wall clearance in the tested pose and travel bounds.

The reduced contact model settled the pipe in the trough, but the installed grip foot and riser intersected its exit path before field contact. Both delivery attempts earn zero points.

Signed pickup-to-trough runs and installed ejection interference · Captured swerve, cam receiver and 337 mm placement stroke

modeled

The forward jack lifts the chassis in a shallow-cage fixture

A registered empty approach at 130 s leaves 4.32 s before powered cutoff. The lowest simulated full-hull carpet clearance is 102.9 mm in the eight tested CG cases.

Cage-plate strength, mounting and inspection mass remain open. The project robot has zero earned climb points.

Climber load path and score decision · Two alliance cages and eight simulated mass-center corners

modeled

The revised receiver extended 370 mm and a released pipe stayed in the trough

Continuous underside lands cleared the two absorber caps. With a 54 mm greater dock setback, 48 modeled launches reached sustained support across both sectors.

The dock was supplied independently. The study assumes a belt exit speed and grants zero match deliveries.

Conditional scoring fixture and 48 supported landings · Two wheel signs, two sectors and three launch times

modeled

The loaded robot braked with its first pipe still aboard

On the two signed wheel paths the fixed camera lost its height bound. Encoders and gyro confirmed a stop at 31.960 or 30.120 s. The pipe moved at most 0.507 or 0.351 mm during each attempt.

These earlier camera-controlled runs finish at their custody-loss stops. The later four-pin receiver starts from its own station capture.

Loaded wheel paths and observed stops · Attained pipe custody on the moving receiver

modeled

The stowed fallback earned five points in both modeled matches

Two empty-start runs at 65 and 72 kg cleared the starting line at the end of AUTO and held their numbered bumper in the red barge zone through assessment. Both runs lasted 156 seconds including disabled time.

The south lane was reserved. Keeping the partner in its usual slot overlaps the starting footprint. The two-pipe scoring route is a separate study.

Stowed fallback with both signed load cases · R4, 156-second continuous traces and native clearance review

modeled

The swerve robot reached the station before the first feed

The corrected drive model reached its docking gate at 20.285 s and 20.330 s for the two 65 kg approaches. Both 72 kg cases also docked before the scheduled 21.100 s feed.

The opening film illustrates the earlier drive model. The corrected first feed and first loaded motion have a separate camera and contact replay.

Opening with signed motor and transmission power · Corrected drive model, four signed mass and calibration cases

modeled

The receiver retained its first pipe through 71.8 mm of swerve travel

All four signed arrival and contact-refinement runs retained the same pipe through finite braking. Both stereo heads agreed in all 88 moving exposures per run under the wheel-angle mask.

Missing a fixed-eye image stopped this version of the drive. The later cam receiver has a separate loaded approach and release record.

Camera-confirmed loaded motion after first feed · R4 with four-module steering occlusion and reciprocal drive model

modeled

Five timely stereo observations confirmed the seated pipe

On the first-feed R4 study, the fixed head located the pipe and the roof head saw its rear edge. Both signed approaches agreed at both simulation time steps.

Matching pipe and shelf finishes hid the rear edge in every required capture. At 45 ms transport delay only three good observations arrived in time. The controller held in both cases.

Simulated stereo observations and delayed frames · R4 first-feed study, two signed approaches and two integration steps

modeled

The R4 inspection budget leaves 170 g of mass margin

The numbered R4 assembly matches the mass register. Four populated modules at their receiving allowance and the specified cable cuts put the upper estimate at 51.993 kg against the 52.163 kg limit.

Uniform one-metre supply cuts put this case 4.9 g over. The mass calculation uses component estimates and planned wire lengths.
